review.reviewer: Claude Code (an AI agent) working for the operator, reading the studies' committed results and the eligibility report; not yet reviewed by the operator
review.disclosure: Every card was written by hand after reading the report's recurring-symptom table, the committed RESULTS files and four check outputs (markup-lite, arm B). The reviewer chose which candidates to write, including ones expected to fail the rules, so the set is not a sample of all possible lessons. Diagnoses are the reviewer's reading of failing assertions, not observed causes. Nothing was generated by a model run for this file.

cards.guidance: For multi-step coding tasks on this model and harness, set a completion cap that does not bind (32,768 rather than Pi's 16,384); a cut-off response wastes the whole trial.
cards.note: The study's pre-registered primary contrast (B − A, +0.41, cluster interval over four paths [+0.09, +0.73]). It acts on the runtime configuration, which MEM-001 fixes at 32,768 in every arm.

cards.guidance: Keep your reasoning brief and move to writing the implementation early.
cards.note: Arm D, the one controlled agent-context intervention in the corpus: a large gain on fetch-cache, none on markup-lite; the pooled interval includes zero. Its mechanism is fewer cut-off responses under a binding cap, which MEM-001 removes.

cards.guidance: Turn thinking off for light tasks: it is several times faster and cheaper per success.
cards.note: Written to test the rule: arm E failed its manipulation check (M6) and the study reports it invalid, so no causal claim may rest on it.

cards.guidance: When parsing inline markup, a code span's content is literal: a backslash inside backticks does not escape the closing backtick, and a run of backticks closes only on a run of the same length.

diagnosis.hypothesis: Implementations that otherwise pass apply backslash escapes inside code spans: three of the four arm-B failures rendered the input `a\` as plain text instead of a\.
alternatives: The fourth arm-B failure is a different mechanism (an unmatched backtick run), so R5 failures are not one cause.

The task's own brief states the rule (R5: inside a code span "no backslash handling"; R7: "any backslash inside a code span is plain text"), and its one visible code-span test has no backslash: the failures are of following a stated interaction between rules that no visible test exercised, so this card repeats the brief rather than adding knowledge.
Every observation is one task (markup-lite); nothing shows the guidance transfers to another parser.

cards.note: The one recurring specific failure in the corpus with reasoning on: every arm-B failure on markup-lite fails R5 alone. All of its evidence is one task (markup-lite), which is development data now (its designated holdout status was spent), and the guidance restates that task's own brief.

cards.guidance: When merging parsed JSON objects, treat a `__proto__` key as ordinary data: copy it with defineProperty or into a null-prototype object, never by assignment.

diagnosis.hypothesis: Without reasoning, implementations merge objects by assignment, which treats `__proto__` as the prototype setter.
alternatives: The arm was invalid (M6); its failures describe what happened, not an effect of turning thinking off.
With reasoning on (arms A, B, D) this check did not fail alone, so the guidance may be unnecessary wherever MEM-001 runs.

cards.note: Observed only with thinking off; MEM-001 keeps reasoning on.

cards.guidance: A cache that returns stored responses must return a fresh copy each time, so a caller's change to one response cannot reach the next caller.

observations.symptom: R7: returned responses are copies, and the URL check stays

diagnosis.hypothesis: Without reasoning, implementations return the stored object itself.
alternatives: With reasoning on, no fetch-cache failure named this check alone.

cards.note: Observed only with thinking off; MEM-001 keeps reasoning on.

cards.guidance: Run every trial with the repository, the research archive and the hidden checks unreachable, and give each trial a private /tmp.
cards.note: The arm-B trial that read the hidden check and the reference solution (excluded by the study). A requirement on the evaluator, not guidance for the agent.

cards.guidance: Hold the workspace path constant within a contrast and vary it only as a registered block: the path alone changed whether a STEER was followed.
cards.note: A rule for designing the experiment (MEM-001 already blocks on path), not guidance for the agent.
